desc: White light flows around each LED slice like liquid. Streaks stretch, taper, split and drain away unpredictably, thinning to fine tips.
Liquid metal running around each slice: rounded silver beads that swell, merge and split, catching a moving highlight.
The same liquid flow in colour: streams of neon whose hue drifts along the outline, with a white-hot core and soft bloom.
Calm liquid streaks until the beat hits: then a surge pours from the top of each slice and races down both sides before draining away.
Two liquid streams, one white and one in an accent colour, weave over and under each other as they flow around every slice.
The liquid outline spills light into each slice: wherever a streak flows, a soft wash bleeds inward and ripples, then fades as the streak moves on.
A premium frosted-glass frame: the clip blurs into the glass band, a soft light glides along the inner edge, and the window casts a gentle shadow inward. Built for keynotes, award shows and concerts.
A fine line of light around the frame with aurora colours flowing along it and soft curtains drifting inward.
Minimal broadcast framing: corner brackets that redraw every 4 bars, a hairline frame, ruler ticks, centre marks and a light that travels the edge.
A liquid-metal frame that flows and ripples on the beat, with thin-film colour and a soft shadow cast onto your content.
A theatre marquee of light bulbs around the frame. The chase pattern changes every bar: run, blink, opposing comets, sparkle.
An energy aura streams off the outline of whoever is on camera, rising and swirling like heat, with colour drifting through it. Kicks flare it up.
Flames rise off the performer’s outline and cool from white-hot to deep red as they climb. Set Flame hue for blue or green fire.
Inspired by aura-camera portraits: soft clouds of colour bloom around the person like a double exposure, with an instant-film finish.
Crackling plasma arcs branch off the performer, flickering between beats and surging outward on every kick.
Glowing embers drift up through a soft halo around the performer, twinkling as they rise. Kicks brighten them.
Outline-shaped rings ripple outward from the performer like sonar, with a bright shock ring on every beat.
Stacked neon outlines trace the performer at growing distances, each its own colour, breathing outward on the beat.
Coloured ghost silhouettes from the last moments trail behind the performer, so every move leaves a spectral echo.
Shafts of light burst outward from behind the performer, a heavenly walk-on glow with a shimmer in the rays.
Turns a live camera into a film: teal-and-orange grade, filmic highlights, red halation glow, grain, gate weave and an optional 2.39 letterbox.
A beauty glow for live feeds: soft diffusion, prism fringes, four-point star glints on highlights, a pastel grade and drifting light leaks.
The live feed as a 90s camcorder tape: line wobble, a rolling tracking band, chroma bleed, tape noise, dropouts, head-switching at the bottom and a blinking REC dot.
Screen-print poster look: posterised duotone, halftone dots, bold outlines and off-register ink. The palette can flip every bar.
Thermal-camera look for live feeds: iron, rainbow or arctic palettes, white-hot or black-hot, a scale bar and crosshair, and a heat pulse on the beat.
The performer as a projected hologram: tinted light, scanlines, edge glow, flicker, glitch tears on the beat, and a projector beam. Dark areas fall away.
The live feed rebuilt as a 3D cloud of glowing points, pushed forward by brightness and orbiting slowly like a volumetric capture. Kicks punch the depth.
The live feed repeated in a grid, each tile a few frames behind the last so movement ripples across the wall. Pop colours per tile, and the order can reshuffle on the beat.
Underwater light caustics dance across the clip and bend it, like the whole stage is at the bottom of a pool.
Deep-water look: caustics on the clip, slanted light shafts falling from the surface and drifting particles.
Caustics split into red, green and blue so every light line carries a rainbow fringe, over a darkened, refracted clip.
Drops land on the beat and send rippling rings across the clip, bending it and catching highlights, over a faint caustic floor.
An organic ink mask that blooms open and closes again over 1, 2, 4 or 8 beats, with a glowing wet edge.
The clip rises out of darkness through drifting smoke and sinks back, with soft lit wisps along the edge.
The clip burns away like paper, with a flame front, charred edge, heat shimmer and embers, then reforms.
Three pigment drops bloom across the frame with dark rims and paper grain, revealing the clip tinted in their colours. New drops each cycle.
The clip shows only through a giant word that punches on the beat. Raise Rows to tile it into scrolling lines.
The frame splits into tiles that flip over in a 3D wave every bar, revealing a hue-shifted back side. The wave origin alternates.
The clip crumbles into glowing particles that blow away on the wind, then reassembles, over 2 to 16 beats.
The scrolling word rows from the Kinetic type source, now as an effect: alternating directions, outline rows, a light sweep, and optional beat-snapped motion. Change the word in Word.
Word rows ride a travelling sine wave while they scroll, like a flag in the wind. Kicks make the wave surge.
The word wrapped around spinning 3D drums, a literal carousel. You see the back of the drum through the gaps.
On every beat a row slams in from alternating sides with overshoot, motion blur and a flash, building a stack.
A solid word at the centre throws a stream of outline copies that grow outward through the colour wheel. Beats push the stream.

Rebuilds the clip as an LED panel with RGB sub-pixels, bloom and a beat ripple. Crossfade to a rotated halftone.
Topographic lines traced from the clip’s brightness, flowing downhill and cycling through the palette.
Traces every outline in the clip as glowing neon tubing, coloured by edge direction, over a dimmed or black background.
Rebuilds the clip from text characters by brightness, with glyph flicker and a beat wave rolling down the screen.
The classic analogue video-synth look: scanlines lifted into 3D by brightness, tilted like a landscape.
Bold black-and-white line fields bent by the clip’s brightness, with moiré interference and a beat pulse rippling outward.
Every frame is fed back into the next, zoomed, rotated and hue-shifted, for endless trails. Key sets what cuts through.
Feedback folded through a kaleidoscope, so the trails grow into a living mandala.
Trails get pulled into a spinning vortex at the centre, cycling colour with every generation. Kicks tighten the spin.
Beat-quantised freeze-frames: copies of the bright parts are stamped on every 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 note and trail behind like a multi-exposure photo.
Feedback pushed through a curl-noise flow field, so the clip smears and swirls like wet paint. Beats stir it harder.
Wet paint running down a wall: trails slide downward at uneven speeds with a sideways wobble.
Orbiting vortices swirl the trails into marbled paper patterns, with the clip combed in as stripes.
The clip feeds a fire: heat rises through curling turbulence and cools from white to yellow to red to black.
Each slice of the frame shows a different moment in the last second, so motion stretches and bends through time.
Red, green and blue each lag by a different number of frames, so anything moving tears into colour ghosts. Beats stretch the gap.
Datamosh-style tiles, each replaying a different moment from the frame buffer, reshuffled on the beat.
B floods in behind an organic liquid front with a glowing rim that bends both pictures as it passes. Set any angle.
A blows out into a bright overexposed flash with bloom and lens streaks, and B emerges from the light. The classic keynote reveal, turned up.
A rockets into the screen with radial blur, a twist and colour split, and B whips back out of it. Punchy for drops.
The frame splits into strips that slide away in alternating directions with a staggered, eased motion and motion blur, carrying B in behind them.
A dissolves into rising smoke and B forms out of it, with soft lit wisps along the edge.
Rows of A smear sideways into pixel-sorted streaks at random times, and B is left behind as they rush off. Clean digital chaos.
B opens out of the centre inside an expanding ring of light that wobbles like liquid and bends both pictures at its edge.
A and B on two faces of a 3D cube that swings round, pulling back mid-turn so you feel the depth, with light falling across the faces.
B burns through A starting from the brightest parts (or the darkest), with a glowing line of light tracing the dissolve.
Red, green and blue tear apart in three directions, each swapping from A to B at its own moment, then snap back together on B.
